request.prompt:
Deliverable: landscape flat technical infographic for a case study about Jev Town.
Primary request: explain local state and partial visibility as a software system. Show a simplified flat town map with five zones, a central square, one red package, twelve small resident markers, and translucent sight boundaries that differ by resident. The main idea is that different state produces different decisions.
Composition: clean top-down map with five labeled zones arranged around the central square. Use simple buildings, paths, docks, and one dark hidden alley. Add a small right-side observation panel with three horizontal probability bars and a tiny decision tree. Use arrows sparingly and keep the visual hierarchy clear.
Style and medium: flat-tech infographic with editorial map language, crisp vector blocks, limited colors, subtle paper texture, no painterly realism, no game HUD.
Text (exact): Render "Jev Town" exactly once as the main title on the top-left. Render "LOCAL STATE" exactly once above the sight-boundary map. Render "PARTIAL VIEW" exactly once above the right-side observation panel. Render "PACKAGE" exactly once beside the red package. No other readable words, numbers, letters, shop signs, or logos anywhere else.
Color: warm off-white background, graphite outlines, muted blue, olive green, vermilion package, pale yellow sight boundaries.
Avoid: fantasy postcard, realistic people, cute mascots, excessive tiny details, duplicated labels, misspellings, watermark.
